title: Background
description: What a character did before adventuring. A background hands out proficiencies, starting gear and one signature feature, then offers roll tables that give the player a personality without inventing one from scratch. Mechanically it is small; most of its weight is the roll tables, so author those carefully.

key.description: Stable slug identifying this background. Derived from the name once and never reused, so saved characters keep resolving after a rename.

name.description: Display name, phrased as the role the character held: Bounty Hunter, Criminal, Jedi.

sourceKey.description: Key of the source this background was published in, matching a document of the source content type. Values present in the archive are phb, wh, snv and ec.

contentSet.description: Whether this background belongs to the core rules or to the community expanded-content supplement.

lore.description: Markdown introduction written to the player, explaining who takes this background and what the life was like. Rules belong in the fields below; this is the pitch.

skillProficiencies.description: The skills granted, as printed. Phrased as an instruction because most backgrounds offer a choice, for example "Choose two from Deception, Insight, Persuasion, and Stealth".

toolProficiencies.description: Kits, gaming sets, instruments or vehicles granted, as printed. Omit when the background grants none.

languageProficiencies.description: Languages granted, as printed. Usually a count the player chooses from rather than named languages. Omit when the background grants none.

startingEquipment.description: Everything the character begins play with, including the credit pouch, as one printed sentence. Item names here should match equipment entries so a character builder can link them.

feature.description: The single narrative privilege the background grants, such as a contact network or safe lodging. Backgrounds grant exactly one, and it is almost always a licence to ask the GM for something rather than a die roll.

name.description: Feature heading, such as Safe Haven or Criminal Contact.

description.description: Markdown rules text, written in second person. Say plainly what the player may ask for and what the limits are, so a GM can adjudicate it without interpretation.

suggestedCharacteristics.description: A short Markdown preamble framing the roll tables that follow: what tends to motivate someone with this history.

personalityTraitOptions.description: Roll table of habits and mannerisms. Entries are descriptions only, written in first person, because a personality trait has no name.

idealOptions.description: Roll table of driving principles. Each entry is named for the ideal and usually closes with the alignment it suits, in parentheses.

bondOptions.description: Roll table of the people, places and obligations the character is tied to. Descriptions only, in first person; these are the hooks a GM pulls on.

flawOptions.description: Roll table of weaknesses and vices. Descriptions only, in first person. A good flaw creates trouble the player wants to play out, not a penalty.

featOptions.description: Roll table of bonus feats appropriate to this history. Entries carry a name only; each name matches a feat entry.

variant.description: An optional specialisation that narrows the background, such as a criminal's speciality or a soldier's rank. Purely flavour: it does not change proficiencies, equipment or the feature.

name.description: Heading for the specialisation, such as Criminal Specialty.

description.description: Markdown explaining what the specialisation covers and how to pick one.

options.description: Roll table of specialisations. Entries carry a name only. Omit when the variant is described in prose without a table.

rollTable.description: A d-something table the player may roll on or choose from. Rolls run from 1 upward with no gaps, and the highest roll is the die size.

roll.description: The die result that selects this entry.

name.description: Short label for the entry. Present on tables whose rows are named things (ideals, feats, specialisations) and absent on tables of free-form statements.

description.description: The entry text. Present on tables of statements the player adopts verbatim; absent when the name is the whole entry.
